column1: # GE-T10's fifth question set (SMYSL-2.5 OQ-22's owed intent vocabulary, second round): sixteen
# questions, two per intent, each asked in the five tier-1 languages, eighty rows, over the
# committed corpus (`../gold/corpus.smy`). Only the front is scored on it, as on `../fourth/`.
# WHY A FIFTH SET. The fourth set's losses were openers the table did not write. The rules for
# them were listed here, exactly, before a word of this set was written, and are scored on this
# set, whose front was taken before the code changed (`baseline.txt`). No rule is added or
# changed after a run of this set; a miss it finds is owed to a sixth.
# THE RULES, DECLARED (from the fourth set's losses only):
#   9. a rule's verb in the past where the table had only the present:
#        en  what depended on / what relied on
#        de  was hing von … ab / was hing vom … ab / was hing von der … ab / woher kam / woher kamen
#        es  qué dependía de / qué dependía del / qué dependían de / de dónde vino / de donde vino /
#        fr  qu'est-ce qui dépendait de / … du / … des / d'où venait / d'où est venu / d'où est venue
#        ru  что зависело от / кто утверждал / кто утверждал что
#  10. other nouns and verbs for evidence:
#        de  gibt es einen nachweis dass / gibt es nachweise dass
#        fr  existe-t-il des preuves que / existe-t-il des preuves qu'
#        en  who believed / who believed in / who believed that
#        de  wer glaubte an / wer glaubte dass
#        es  quién creía en / quien creía en / quién creía que
#        fr  qui croyait à / qui croyait au / qui croyait aux / qui croyait en / qui croyait que
#        ru  кто верил в / кто верил что
#  12. other verbs for where a subject is mentioned:
#        es  dónde se habla de / dónde se habla del / donde se habla de
#        fr  où parle-t-on de / où parle-t-on du / où parle-t-on des
#        en  what precisely is / what precisely was (define), what made (explain),
#        ru  что представляет собой / что представлял собой / что представляли собой (define)
# WHO WROTE THIS. The same hand that declared the rules, after declaring them, so it knew them;
# the questions are written as a person would ask, and half of them reach for an opener none of
# the rules writes (another tense, another verb, another construction), which is expected to
# fail. Nothing was rephrased after a run. Single hand, so no agreement figure.
# Columns as `../gold/questions.tsv`: qid, intent, lang, question.
